thread.title: Jabil strikes deal with Johnson & Johnson that could grow revenue by more than $1 billion

author: Ashley Gurbal Kritzer
title: Jabil strikes deal with Johnson & Johnson that could grow revenue by more than $1 billion
text: – Senior Reporter, Tampa Bay Business Journal Sep 25, 2018, 6:37pm EDT Jabil Inc. has struck a deal with Johnson & Johnson Medical Devices Cos. that CEO Mark Mondello says could be "transformational" for the St. Petersburg-based electronics manufacturer. On an earnings call Tuesday, Mondello said Jabil (NYSE: JBL) has entered into a partnership with Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) that covers endoscopy, surgical, spine, trauma and instrumentation devices. "Integration cost and charges directly associated with the deal will be in the range of $80 million. The real interesting part about this deal is that the cash outlay will largely be applied to working capital and inventory," Mondello said on the call. "We believe the annual revenue will grow to an excess of $1 billion annually." A Jabil spokesman was not immediately available for comment Tuesday. Jabil will acquire 14 sites in the deal, Mondello said. News of the partnership was reported last week in the Swiss press, as the deal affects seven sites in Switzerland, reports Neue Zürcher Zeitung, a newspaper based in Zurich. Nearly a quarter of Jabil's sales in 2017 came from Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL), as Jabil makes casings for iPhones. Jabil is one of the largest employers in the Tampa Bay region. It is expanding its global headquarters in St. Petersburg at Roosevelt Boulevard and Dr. Martin Luther King Street North.
